# Data Exploration

- What can you quantify? 
- What can you observe for close analysis?
- What questions would you like to answer?

## What's in our data?

- What types of data do we have? 
	- | numeric | categoric | geographic | relationships | temporal
- How many variables do we have? 
- How do our variables relate to each other? 
	- | quantities/distribution | correlation | part of a whole | change over time | relationships
- What questions can we ask of this dataset?

## Data types

WTF CSV: a tool for basic data summaries - [databasic.io/wtfcsv](https://www.databasic.io/es/wtfcsv/)

- Download the dataset as a csv 
- Upload it into [WTF CSV](https://www.databasic.io/en/wtfcsv/) (or use this link: [GCSFI in WTF CSV](https://www.databasic.io/en/wtfcsv/results/6adf65e435cec4457e7aa401))
- What do you notice? What can you observe here? 

## Relationships

Nineteen: simple count visualizations - [usenineteen.com](https://usenineteen.com/)

- Upload the dataset as a csv
- What categories can we compare?
- What do you notice about the results?

## Text fields

Voyant: a tool for text analysis and visualization - [voyant-tools.org](https://voyant-tools.org/)

- Try visualizing one column at a time
- Stopwords: select 'Spanish'

# Data visualization

Wednesday, October 28

## Data visualization process {background-color="white"}

```{mermaid}
graph LR
	A(Collect data) --> B(Clean & <br>document data)
	C(Find a<br> dataset)--> B
	B-->D[Analyze<br>data]
	D-->H(Decide what<br> to show)
	H-->E(Choose <br>visualization<br>type)
	E-->I(Customize it)
	H-->F(Design a viz<br> from scratch)
	F-->G(Tell the <br>data story)
	I-->G
```
## Next steps

What types of cleaning, organization, or summarizing do we need to do?

- Simple accuracy?
- Improved machine-readability?
- Analysis and summary?
- Bringing in context?

# Data Cleaning

- Numbers, dates, geocoordinates
- Standardizing spelling and controlled terms
- Creating new columns
- Adding contextual data

# Choosing visualizations

[from Data to Viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/)

## Planning a visualization

- What will you show? 
- What graph types would best communicate your data story?
- How will you design your visualization?

## What will you show?

- All variables?
- Relationships between variables? 
- Summaries? Every data point?

## What type of graph?

- Useful resource: [From Data to Viz](https://www.data-to-viz.com/)
- Use your imagination! Draw your visualization on paper.
- For inspiration: [Dear Data project](http://www.dear-data.com/theproject), Georgia Lupi & Stefanie Posavec; the winners of the [Information is Beautiful Awards](https://www.informationisbeautifulawards.com/)

## Design considerations

- What methods can you use to convey your variables?
- How can you make the results visually compelling and communicative?
- How can you make them more accessible?
